title: Crucial Conversations for Mastering Dialogue
transcript: Language is our first tool, our first technology, the very thing that makes us human. And it’s a kind of power, a power that’s frequently misunderstood and poorly used. Most conversations involve little risk. We go about our days chatting, discussing, working, connecting, agreeing, and then every so often we encounter conflict. The boss shuts down your idea. Your direct report refuses. Your child disobeys. It’s in the face of disagreement where people struggle most to communicate effectively. And it’s in the face of disagreement where we have the greatest opportunity to influence the outcomes we care about. You can strengthen relationships and get better results through communication. It largely depends on how well you handle Crucial Conversations.

title: How Do I Start a Crucial Conversation?
